title: The Impossible Songbook
premise: Tamsin Whitlock, a single father hiding from a scandal that ended his music career, runs the only bookshop in the coastal town of Marrow Bay and has spent three years being no one in particular. When the town's autumn festival pairs residents into anonymous pen-pal exchanges, he is matched with Vivian Ash, the festival organizer who once testified against him—and neither realizes the sharp, funny letters they're falling for belong to their worst enemy. As the correspondence deepens and identities unravel, Tamsin must choose between the safe invisibility he's built for his daughter and the truth that could cost him everything again. At the festival's closing night, he performs the songbook he swore never to touch, forgives the man in the mirror, and chooses love over silence.
about_author: Odile Vane is the pen name of a former choir teacher who now writes love stories from a drafty cottage on the northern coast. She believes every small town keeps one secret worth singing about.

chapters.title: The Shelf Nobody Browses
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. We meet him three years after his career collapsed: running Whitlock's Books, raising his daughter Wren, and carefully invisible. The festival committee arrives with pen-pal sign-up slips; his daughter signs him up before he can refuse. Emotional beat: quiet dread beneath practiced calm.

chapters.title: Dear Stranger
chapters.summary: Alternating POV begins. Tamsin receives his first letter—wry, probing, annoyingly perceptive—and fires back something sharper than intended. Meanwhile Vivian Ash drafts her own opening letter, wrestling with guilt she won't name. Emotional beat: sparks disguised as friction.

chapters.title: What Vivian Knew
chapters.summary: Vivian's POV flashback. Three years ago she was the young organizer who confirmed the allegations against composer Tam Whitlock, ending his career. She never learned the full story behind what she signed. Now she organizes the festival that haunts them both. Emotional beat: buried remorse stirring.

chapters.title: Letters Like Small Fires
chapters.summary: Both POVs. The exchange turns intimate—fears, failures, first loves confessed to strangers. Tamsin catches himself checking the mail like a teenager; Vivian rereads his letters at her desk instead of working. Emotional beat: warmth neither will admit to.

chapters.title: The Man at the Bake Sale
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. A near-miss: Tamsin and Vivian clash publicly over festival logistics, each complaining about their 'impossible' pen pal to the other without knowing it. Wren notices her father humming again for the first time in years. Emotional beat: dramatic irony tightening the screws.

chapters.title: Half a Truth
chapters.summary: Vivian's POV. Digging into old case files for the festival's anniversary exhibit, Vivian finds discrepancies in the testimony she gave—including evidence that Tamsin took the fall for someone else. She starts pulling threads. Emotional beat: loyalty to her old allies versus growing doubt.

chapters.title: The Name in the Margin
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. Vivian, unknowingly, quotes one of his lyrics in a letter; he recognizes himself in her words and realizes who she is—the woman who ended his life as he knew it. He stops writing but can't stop reading. Emotional beat: betrayal curdling into longing.

chapters.title: Everything Except the Ending
chapters.summary: Both POVs converge. Vivian discovers the truth of the scandal and confronts the man who actually forged the documents; Tamsin, cornered by Wren's questions about why he stopped writing, nearly burns the letters. They finally recognize each other at the festival setup—pen pals and enemies at once. Emotional beat: collision.

chapters.title: Closing Night
chapters.summary: Climax, both POVs. At the festival finale, the exhibit exposes the real culprit publicly. Called out by name, Tamsin must decide in front of the whole town: retreat or answer. He takes the stage, opens the impossible songbook, and sings—for Wren, for Vivian, for the man he buried. Emotional beat: reckoning turned release.

chapters.title: Second Chances, Better Timing
chapters.summary: Resolution, Tamsin's POV with a final letter from Vivian. Weeks later, the bookshop hosts a small concert; the songbook sells from the shelf nobody browsed. Tamsin writes Vivian one last letter and delivers it by hand. Emotional beat: forgiveness earned, love chosen, identity reclaimed.
